samples.summary: Scope creep: a backend security-posture default flip (shadow → enforce) plus a brand-new `yorkie-service` identity are bundled into a share-link notes-toolbar PR (issue #1044). The issue's scope list (`docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md` N1–N8 + divider + docs) contains none of this, and `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` had *decided* the opposite ("Shadow mode (default)" as rollout step 2, Goal: "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)"). The cost is outside the codebase: any existing deployment that registered the webhook methods and left the variable unset (the documented shadow posture) starts denying traffic on upgrade with no config change — exactly the staged-rollout risk the design doc's step 2 existed to absorb — and every server-side attach now depends on the new service token being minted correctly. Whether or not enforce-by-default is right, it is a separate architectural decision that deserves its own change and its own rollout note, not a rider on a UI parity fix.
samples.evidence: New `isYorkieAuthEnforced` inverts the documented default; `docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md` scope (N1–N8, divider, docs) never mentions webhook enforcement or a service token.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim copy of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` (issue #989): same allowlist-of-readers rationale, same memoization map, same `get` non-configurable exception, and the same eight traps (`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`) with the same comments. Only the readers set, `HISTORY_METHODS`, and the idempotence `WeakSet` differ. This repo expects shared logic to live in `@wafflebase/core` (docs already depends on it), and this is security-relevant trap logic: the next escape-hatch fix (a trap somebody forgot, e.g. the `WeakSet` idempotence that notes added and docs lacks — docs' wrapper is *not* idempotent) will land in one copy only, so the two boundaries give different answers to the same question. A generic `readOnlyStoreView(store, readers, overrides)` in core, consumed by both engines, was the available reuse.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-168 vs packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:99-185 — identical trap set and comments; notes adds READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotence that docs lacks.

samples.summary: The enforce-by-default flip is recorded in `yorkie-auth-webhook.md` and `notes/notes.md` but the other canonical design docs that assert the old default were left contradicting it, so the design corpus now gives two answers to "is enforcement on by default?". `docs/design/sharing.md:208-219` still says "This is **off by default**… the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary" (the exact claim `notes/notes.md` now records as wrong), `sharing.md:233` repeats it, and `docs/design/template-gallery.md:668` says "with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*". Repo discipline is to fold a correction into the canonical subsystem doc, not to correct one doc and leave its siblings stale — and these are the docs a reviewer consults when judging whether a client-side gate is load-bearing.
samples.evidence: sharing.md:208 "This is **off by default**"; template-gallery.md:668 "with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*"; docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301 same premise.

samples.summary: Sibling source comments still document the old default and the old (now explicitly retracted) claim that the client-side wrapper is the write boundary: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40` ("ships in shadow mode by default … this flag is the write boundary") and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413` ("shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`"). The notes copy of the same comment was rewritten in this diff; the docs original was not, so the two engines' read-only wrappers now describe opposite deployment defaults.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42 vs packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-70 ("the earlier claim here … was wrong").

samples.summary: The diff adds a comment saying this check is "the same explicit affirmation the server demands at submit/approve — see assertYorkieAuthEnforced", but keeps the inline `config.get(...) !== 'true'` rather than calling `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` from `src/template/template-review.ts`. Three readings of one variable now exist (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`, `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`, this inline compare); the seed copy will silently diverge from the gate it claims to mirror the next time the gate's rule changes.
samples.evidence: register-templates.ts:157 inline compare while template-review.ts:89 exports the shared assertion the comment cites.

samples.summary: The read-only store is wrapped in two places — `initialize()` in the engine and again at the frontend mount — with idempotence added to make the double-wrap harmless. Defensible, but it puts the same responsibility at two layers; if the engine is the owner of the guarantee (it now is, per the design doc), the frontend wrap is redundant belt-and-braces whose only justification is that neither layer can see the other.

verdict.reason: Verified present and reachable. `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22) makes unset mean ENFORCE and is consumed by the live webhook handler (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:133-134) and template service (packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:470). The brand-new `yorkie-service` identity exists (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts:27-87) and is wired into YorkieService (yorkie.service.ts:55) and three ops scripts. The originating issue's scope (docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:12-38, N1-N8 + divider + notes docs) contains no mention of webhook enforcement or a service token, and the paired lessons doc does not either. The prior decision was the opposite: docs/design/sharing.md:208 and archive/2026/07/20260712-yorkie-auth-webhook-todo.md:26 still record shadow-by-default, and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:43 retains the Goal "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)" while :221 now says "Enforce (the default)". .agent-review/docs/summary.md:3 confirms the flip and its env-var doc updates are part of this diff, not pre-existing. No guard makes it inert: a deployment that followed the previously documented path (register methods, leave the variable unset = shadow) begins denying on upgrade with no config change, and every server-side attach now depends on the new token. That is a cost outside the codebase's own tidiness, meeting the major bar for scope past a recorded design decision. No refutation ground applies: code is present as described, unguarded, and squarely in the design-fit lane.

verdict.reason: The claimed duplication is present and the cited evidence is accurate. packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93-185 reproduces packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 almost verbatim: same memoization Map of {raw,view}, same non-configurable/non-writable `get` exception (docs:84-87 vs notes:112-115), same hide-non-function-data-property rule (docs:96 vs notes:117), same `batch` grouping-seam carve-out with near-identical comment (docs:104-112 vs notes:127-136), and the identical ten traps set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions/isExtensible/has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys (docs:122-167 vs notes:149-180) with several comments word-for-word. The claimed divergence is also real: notes adds READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotence (notes:43,94,183) that docs lacks entirely, so the two copies of this security-relevant trap logic have already begun to drift. Reuse was genuinely available: @wafflebase/core exists as the shared package (packages/core/src/{geometry,tokens,url,image}) and docs already depends on it (packages/docs/package.json:56). I considered refuting on `counterexample` via the stated Non-Goal in docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48 ("Store abstraction unification ... No common base proposed here", Tier C at :84) plus the fact that notes has no core dependency (packages/notes/package.json:52-71) — but that Non-Goal concerns unifying the three store *interfaces*/model types, not a generic reader-allowlist proxy utility, so it does not cleanly cover the proposed extraction. docs/design/notes/notes.md:289-291 documents the file as "the sibling of packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts" but records no decision against sharing. Duplication/reuse is squarely this lens's lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply either. No named ground refutes the finding.
